issues.legal_issue: A widow’s adoption under a legal system requiring her deceased husband’s authority is invalid when that authority has not been proved.
material_facts: The parties were governed by a school of Hindu law under which a widow could not adopt without authority from her deceased husband.
The widow performed the adoption ceremonies, but the evidence of witnesses did not establish that her husband had authorized her to adopt.

The widow later executed a deed of adoption reciting her husband’s desire and applied to be appointed guardian of the child, but there was no evidence that she knew her husband’s authority was legally required.
issues.conclusion: The husband’s authority was not proved, so the adoption was invalid; the widow was entitled to her deceased husband’s full one-third share in the joint family properties.
issues.legal_principle: Under the applicable Banaras School of Hindu Law, a widow could not adopt a son without her deceased husband’s authority. The party relying on the adoption had to establish that authority. The widow’s performance of the adoption ceremonies, the deed’s recital, and her guardianship application did not establish authority where she may have acted believing the adoption was valid and there was no evidence she knew authority was required. The judgment relies on no earlier cases or statutory provisions.

rule.if: partition_appeal and widow_adoption_disputed and governing_law_requires_husbands_authority and not husbands_authority_proven

predicates.partition_appeal: The dispute arose in an appeal from a partition proceeding.
predicates.widow_adoption_disputed: A party disputed the validity of an adoption made by a widow.
predicates.governing_law_requires_husbands_authorit: The legal system governing the parties required a widow to have her deceased husband’s authority to adopt.
predicates.husbands_authority_proven: Evidence established that the deceased husband authorized the widow to adopt.

issues.definition: When a partition appeal disputes a widow’s adoption, the governing law requires her deceased husband’s authority, and that authority is not proved, the adoption is invalid.
